hypotheses.reasoning: Earliest anomaly is at notif-db: at 12:41:09Z a transaction (93036) owned by template-svc-reconciler had been ACTIVE for 82s while holding a row lock on notifications with only 1 undo entry, i.e. it was open and idle, not doing real work. Lock waits then build: notif-db 'Lock wait timeout exceeded' on UPDATE notifications (#1237, #1255). template-svc's UPDATEs on notifications hit statement_timeout (#1267, #1310). notification-svc then gets ReadTimeout/render timeouts calling template-svc (#1270, #1314), its pool to template-svc is exhausted (#1428), and api-gateway returns 504s (#1362, #1503). Before 12:39:47 template-svc /render calls completed in roughly 30-85ms, so the lock was the first fault. Ruled out: metrics-agent remote-write queue saturation (#347, #599) is a noisy but unrelated symptom, and billing-reconciler logged 0 discrepancies throughout. The logs don't show why the reconciler transaction was left open, so the exact trigger (a hung reconciler call or an uncommitted transaction) is unconfirmed.

Connection pool from notification-svc to template-svc is exhausted (#1428), which could be read as pool-limit exhaustion. However, the pool only saturates because calls hang behind the DB lock, so this is a symptom of the dependency_timeout above, not its origin.

Retries and timeouts amplify the lock stall across notification-svc, template-svc and the gateway. The trigger is the database lock, so this is downstream amplification rather than the originating fault.

verdict.recommendedAction: Kill the idle-in-transaction session holding the notifications row lock (transaction 93036, template-svc-reconciler) on notif-db, then verify lock waits and template-svc statement timeouts clear. Fix the reconciler to commit or roll back promptly and enforce an idle-in-transaction timeout. Add shorter timeouts and pool limits on notification-svc calls to template-svc so a single stuck lock does not cascade to 504s at the gateway.
